Quotes that settle the passing cards:

- sr1-02: "Default configuration does not merge with job configuration. If the job already has a keyword defined, the job keyword takes precedence" (/ci/yaml/#default).

- sr1-04: under inherit:variables, "a list indicates which specific variables are inherited by that job" (/ci/jobs/#control-the-inheritance-of-default-keywords-and-variables).
- sr1-05: "If `stages` is not defined ... the default pipeline stages are: .pre, build, test, deploy, .post".

Minor points, not flagged:
- sr1-07 is the easiest card. Its hedge "can ... when runners are available" leans toward True. Its explanation's phrase "share an execution level" is not GitLab terminology; "Stages run in sequence, while the jobs in a stage run in parallel" would read better.
- sr1-01 could be sharper as "The order in which jobs appear in .gitlab-ci.yml decides which job of a stage starts first". As written, an expert would still answer False.

The YAML reference (https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/yaml/#after_script) says the same: "Don't affect the job's exit code. If the script section succeeds and the after_script times out or fails, the job exits with code 0". But https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/runners/configure_runners/#ignore-errors-in-after_script says: "By default, GitLab Runner ignores any errors that happen when after_script runs. To set the job to fail immediately on errors when after_script runs, set the AFTER_SCRIPT_IGNORE_ERRORS CI/CD variable to false." The runner source (gitlab-runner common/build.go) confirms this: when AfterScriptIgnoreErrors is false and the script succeeded, `err = afterScriptErr` and the job fails.
flagged.problem: The statement has no 'by default'. Any job can set the documented CI/CD variable AFTER_SCRIPT_IGNORE_ERRORS: false, and then an after_script failure does fail a job whose script succeeded. An expert can defend True.
flagged.suggestedFix: Answer stays false. Statement: "By default, an `after_script` failure marks a job as failed even when its `script` section succeeded." Explanation: "GitLab Runner ignores after_script errors by default, so the job keeps its script result. Setting the AFTER_SCRIPT_IGNORE_ERRORS variable to false lets an after_script error fail the job." Add https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/runners/configure_runners/#ignore-errors-in-after_script as the source, or keep job_execution and mention the variable.
